summary: Chinese never changes the adjective to compare: it adds words. ‘Taller than’ is A 比 B + adjective — 我哥哥比我高 ‘my brother is taller than me’ — with the adjective bare (no 很). How much more follows the adjective (高一点 ‘a bit taller’, 快多了 ‘much faster’, 大两岁 ‘two years older’); 更 or 还 before it says ‘even more’. ‘Not as … as’ is A 没有 B + adjective (我没有他高), ‘as … as’ is A 跟 B 一样 + adjective (我跟他一样高). 更 + adjective is ‘more …’ when the other thing is understood (这个更好 ‘this one is better’), and 最 + adjective is ‘the most …’ (他最高 ‘he is the tallest’, 最好的饭馆 ‘the best restaurant’).

head: Meaning
Pattern
Example
rows: 我哥哥比我高。 My brother is taller than me.
A 比 B + adjective + 多了
飞机比火车快多了。 Planes are much faster than trains.
A 比 B + adjective + 一点
这个比那个贵一点。 This one is a bit dearer than that one.
我比我妹妹大两岁。 I’m two years older than my sister.
A 比 B + 更 / 还 + adjective
今天比昨天更冷。 Today is even colder than yesterday.
我没有我哥哥高。 I’m not as tall as my brother.
A 跟 B 一样 + adjective
我跟他一样高。 I’m as tall as him.
这个更好。 This one is better.
他最高。 He is the tallest.
blocks.caption: Comparing: the adjective never changes
A 比 B + adjective — the adjective stays bare

blocks.title: No 很 after 比
blocks.text: *他比我很高 → 他比我高. To make it stronger, put 更 / 还 before the adjective (他比我还高 ‘even taller’) or 多了 after it (高多了 ‘much taller’).

blocks.title: The negative: 没有, not 不比
blocks.text: 他没有我高 ‘he is not as tall as me’ is the normal negative. 他不比我高 means ‘he is no taller than me’ — it corrects someone (we are about the same).

blocks.title: The amount goes after the adjective
blocks.text: 大两岁 ‘two years older’, 贵一点 ‘a bit dearer’, 快多了 ‘much faster’ — the quality first, then how much.

items.title: 更 — more
points: 这个更好。 This one is better.
我更喜欢茶。 I prefer tea.

items.title: 最 — the most
points: 这是最好的饭馆。 This is the best restaurant.
我最喜欢蓝色。 Blue is my favourite colour.

blocks.title: No -er, no -est
blocks.text: 高 · 比他高 · 更高 · 最高 — the adjective never changes. German changes the word (größer, am größten); Chinese adds a word.

blocks.title: Questions
blocks.text: 他比你高吗？ ‘Is he taller than you?’ · 哪个更便宜？ ‘Which one is cheaper?’ · 谁最高？ ‘Who is the tallest?’

blocks.title: Comparing without 比
blocks.text: Two bare adjectives already contrast: 这个大，那个小 ‘this one is bigger, that one smaller’.

blocks.title: Three words do it all
blocks.text: 比 brings in what you compare with, 更 ‘more’ and 最 ‘most’ stand before the adjective, and the adjective itself never changes: 比我高, 更高, 最高.

blocks.title: Colours: light and dark
blocks.text: 浅 ‘light’ and 深 ‘dark’ go straight before the colour: 浅蓝色 ‘light blue’, 深绿色 ‘dark green’. Colour nouns take 的 before a noun (红色的车) and 是…的 as a predicate (车是红色的); the one-syllable colours join a noun directly (红葡萄酒).

askYourself: Am I comparing two things? → A 比 B + adjective.
Did I put 很 or 非常 after 比? → remove it: use 更 / 还 before the adjective, or 多了 / 一点 after it.
How much more? → after the adjective: 一点, 多了, or a number (大两岁).
Is it negative? → A 没有 B + adjective (‘not as … as’).
Are they equal? → A 跟 B 一样 + adjective.
The most of a group? → 最 + adjective (the group first: 我们家我爸爸最高).
Only one thing named, the other understood? → 更 + adjective (这个更好).
steps: Then, if needed, how much (一点, 多了, 两岁).

traps: *他比我不高 → 他没有我高.
*他比我一点高 → 他比我高一点 (the amount after the adjective).
*我跟他一样很高 → 我跟他一样高.
*最很好, *更很好 → 最好, 更好.
他不比我高 (‘not taller — about the same’) ≠ 他没有我高 (‘not as tall’).
Older than (people) is 大, not 老: 他比我大两岁.

quiz.why: A 比 B + the bare adjective — no 很.

quiz.q: ‘I’m not as tall as my brother.’
quiz.why: The negative comparison is A 没有 B + adjective.

quiz.q: ‘He is two years older than me.’
quiz.why: The amount follows the adjective, and age uses 大.
最 goes before the verb or adjective it raises to the top.
A 跟 B 一样 + the bare adjective.
‘Much more’ is 多了 after the adjective.
浅 ‘light’ goes straight before the colour; dark blue is 深蓝色.

notes.text: Greek has an analytic comparative too (πιο ψηλός ‘more tall’ ~ 更高) besides ψηλότερος, but ‘than’ (από) follows the adjective: πιο ψηλός από μένα. Chinese puts 比 + the other thing before it: 比我高.
Russian выше / дороже change the adjective and put ‘than’ after it (выше меня); Chinese adds 比 before an unchanged adjective: 比我高. самый ~ 最.
Spanish más alto que yo is analytic like Chinese (más ~ 更, el más alto ~ 最高), but que + the other thing follows the adjective; Chinese puts 比 + the other thing first: 比我高.

English taller / tallest change the adjective and ‘than’ follows it (taller than me); Chinese puts 比 + the other thing before an unchanged adjective: 比我高. ‘not as tall as’ ~ 没有…高; ‘as tall as’ ~ 跟…一样高.
French plus grand que moi is analytic like Chinese (plus ~ 更, le plus ~ 最), but que + the other thing follows the adjective; Chinese: 比我高.
German größer als ich changes the adjective and puts als after it; Chinese 比我高 adds 比 before an unchanged adjective. am größten ~ 最高.
Hindi puts the thing compared with first, with से, and leaves the adjective unchanged: वह मुझसे लंबा है ~ 他比我高. सबसे ‘than all’ ~ 最: सबसे लंबा ~ 最高.
Persian adds -tar to the adjective and az ‘than’ after it (bozorgtar az man ‘bigger than me’); Chinese leaves the adjective unchanged and puts 比 + the other thing first: 比我大.
Marathi puts the other thing first with -पेक्षा and leaves the adjective unchanged: तो माझ्यापेक्षा उंच आहे ~ 他比我高; सगळ्यात ‘of all’ ~ 最.
Arabic makes a new form of the adjective (kabīr → akbar) and puts min ‘than’ after it (akbar minnī ‘bigger than me’); Chinese leaves 大 alone and puts 比 + the other thing first: 比我大.
Hebrew yoter gadol mi- ‘more big than’ is analytic like 更大, but mi- follows the adjective; Chinese puts 比 first: 比我大. ha-khi gadol ~ 最大.
Turkish also keeps the adjective unchanged and puts the other thing first: benden daha uzun ‘taller than me’ (-den ~ 比, daha ~ 更), en uzun ~ 最高.
Japanese 私より高い ‘taller than me’ puts the other thing first, with より, and leaves the adjective unchanged — the Chinese 比我高 with the particle after the noun. 一番 / 最も ~ 最.
Korean 나보다 커요 ‘bigger than me’ puts the other thing first with 보다 and leaves the adjective unchanged; 더 ~ 更, 제일 ~ 最.
Finnish adds -mpi to the adjective (pitkä → pidempi) with kuin ‘than’ after it, or puts the other thing first in the partitive (minua pidempi); Chinese never changes the adjective: 比我高.
Hungarian adds -bb to the adjective (magas → magasabb) and marks the other thing with -nál / -nél or mint; Chinese never changes the adjective: 比我高. leg-…-bb ~ 最.
Swahili says ‘tall more than me’: mrefu kuliko mimi; Chinese puts the other thing first: 比我高.
Luganda compares with the verb ‘to surpass’ (-singa) after the adjective; Chinese 比 also comes from a verb (‘to compare’), but stands before the adjective: 比我高.
Vietnamese puts hơn ‘more than’ after the adjective (cao hơn tôi ‘taller than me’) and nhất after it for ‘most’ (cao nhất); Chinese puts 比 and 最 before it: 比我高, 最高.
Inuktitut makes the comparative with a suffix inside the word, and the thing compared with takes a ‘from’ ending; Chinese uses separate words and an unchanged adjective: 比我高.

seeAlso.note: German changes the adjective: größer als, am größten / der größte (with umlaut); Chinese leaves 大 as it is and adds 比 before the second thing and 最 before the adjective.

Arabic builds a new form from the root, the elative أَفْعَلُ + مِنْ (أَكْبَرُ مِنْ ‘bigger than’), which also serves as the superlative (أَكْبَرُ بَيْتٍ ‘the biggest house’); Chinese uses separate words, 比 and 最.
Hebrew, like Chinese, adds words and leaves the adjective unchanged: יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל מִ… ‘bigger than’, הֲכִי גָּדוֹל ‘the biggest’ — 更 / 比 and 最 do the same jobs.
The bare adjective (without 很) is the comparison form: 他比我高.
没有 (S08) is also the negative of a comparison: 我没有他高.
